body:
`Series.replace`/`DataFrame.replace` silently discarded a compiled `re.Pattern` on arrow-backed string dtypes:

```python
pd.Series(["a", "b"], dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.string())).replace(re.compile("^a"), "z")
# ['a', 'b']   <- discarded; object, str, string[python] and string[pyarrow] all substitute
```

`Block._replace_regex` gated compiled patterns on a literal allowlist, `_regex_target_dtype(self.dtype) not in [object, "string"]`. `ArrowDtype(pa.string())` matches neither, so the pattern never reached `replace_regex`. The string spelling of the same pattern was unaffected — `is_re("^a")` is False, so it never hit the guard.

The allowlist is now `is_string_dtype(target) and target.kind != "S"`. The `kind != "S"` half keeps numpy bytes out, since `is_string_dtype` counts them and a regex can never match bytes (without it a `|S2` Series silently upcast to `object` on what is still a no-op). The predicate is still applied to `_regex_target_dtype`, which resolves a `Categorical` to its categories' dtype (GH-68928), so a `Categorical` of arrow strings stops being a silent no-op too.

A compiled pattern now takes the same path as the string spelling, including its upcast to `object` for a replacement an arrow string column can't hold (GH-70458).

Not covered here, each a separate defect with its own review surface: dictionary-encoded arrow strings, which `is_string_dtype` rejects, and `pa.string_view()`, where the direct path discards silently just as `string` did while the `regex=` dict path raises `NotImplementedError` from `ArrowDtype.type`, so admitting it to `is_string_dtype` would not be enough. Also, non-regex `replace` makes the same always-fits check and still raises for a value that doesn't fit (`ser.replace("a", 1)`), so the regex and non-regex spellings disagree until that is fixed separately.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5 (high)`), which wrote the fix, the tests and this description; reviewed and verified by me.
title: BUG: replace silently discards a compiled regex on ArrowDtype strings
